name: Build and Test

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: '**'

jobs:
  docker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - run: npm ci

      - run: npm run lint

      - run: npm test

      - run: npm run build

apiVersion: 1

providers:
  - name: load-tester
    orgId: 1
    folder: ''
    type: file
    disableDeletion: false
    updateIntervalSeconds: 30
    options:
      path: /etc/grafana/provisioning/dashboards

{
  "annotations": {
    "list": [
      {
        "builtIn": 1,
        "datasource": "-- Grafana --",
        "enable": true,
        "hide": true,
        "iconColor": "rgba(0, 211, 255, 1)",
        "name": "Annotations & Alerts",
        "type": "dashboard"
      }
    ]
  },
  "editable": true,

        "y": 1

      "id": 101,
      "options": {
        "content": "| Panel | What the numbers are | Timeframe |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Connected clients and logins** | Open DDP websocket connections, plus login successes and failures | Connections are a live value. Login series are running totals since the run started, so they only climb |\n| **Action rate** | Actions completed per second, per action type | Mean over a trailing 5 minutes |\n| **Actions completed** | Total actions per action type, with separate error series | Cumulative since the tester started. Resets if it restarts |\n| **Action duration** | Mean wall clock time for one action to complete | Mean over a trailing 5 minutes |\n\n**Reading it:** compare the action rate against the events per second printed in the tester's startup log. Rates below the configured value, or durations rising while the rate falls, mean the workspace is saturating. Climbing error series in *Actions completed* mean failures are accumulating.\n\n**Diagnostics, when something looks wrong:**\n\n- **REST errors by endpoint** is the first place to look. Empty is healthy. Rejected or failing requests appear here even though the tester suppresses most action errors and still reports users as logged in.\n- **REST latency by endpoint** separates the individual calls inside one action, so you can tell which endpoint is slow rather than which action.\n- **Stream subscriptions** covers DDP subscribe health, a separate failure mode from REST. Subscribe failures usually mean a login sequence was cut short.\n- **Action duration p99** shows the tail. A p99 climbing while the mean is flat is an early warning.\n- **Load generator health** is a collapsed row at the bottom. Open it before blaming the workspace: if event loop lag there is above roughly 50 milliseconds, or CPU is near 1.0 core, the tester is the bottleneck and these numbers no longer measure Rocket.Chat.\n\n**Caveats:**\n\n- `sendMessage` includes a deliberate one second typing pause, so a mean near one second is by design, not server latency.\n- Durations are measured client side, so they include network and reverse proxy time.\n- Action counts are not server request counts: one `openRoom` drives several requests and also triggers a `read`, while a presence action with nothing new to subscribe to sends none.",
        "mode": "markdown"
      },

      "type": "text"

name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'main'
    tags:
      - '*.*.*'

jobs:
  docker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - run: npm ci

      - run: npm run lint

      - run: npm test

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v2

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      - name: Docker meta
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v4
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/rocketchat/rocket.chat.load.tester
          tags: |
            type=ref,event=branch
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
            type=sha

      - name: Login to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v3
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}

# rocket.chat.load.tester

## Requirements

- Node v10+

## How to use

```
npm i
npm start
```

## Configurations via environment variables

Rate values are in "per day per user".

| Env var name               | Mandatory | Default value               | Description                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HOST_URL`                 | **Yes**   | `localhost:3000`            | Rocket.Chat URL                                                                           |
| `DATABASE_URL`             | **Yes**   | `mongodb://localhost:27017` | MongoDB connection string                                                                 |
| `DATABASE_NAME`            | **Yes**   | `rocketchat`                | MongoDB database name                                                                     |
| `PORT`                     | No        | `4000`                      | The port this service will listen to                                                      |
| `HOW_MANY_USERS`           | No        | `10`                        | How many simultaneous connections                                                         |
| `LOGIN_BATCH`              | No        | `5`                         | Simultaneous logins                                                                       |
| `MESSAGE_SENDING_RATE`     | No        | `100`                       | Message sending rate (100 messages per day per user)                                      |
| `SET_STATUS_RATE`          | No        | `10`                        | Set status rate                                                                           |
| `OPEN_ROOM_RATE`           | No        | `10`                        | Open room rate                                                                            |
| `READ_MESSAGE_RATE`        | No        | `10`                        | Read message rate                                                                         |
| `SUBSCRIBE_PRESENCE_RATE`  | No        | `100`                       | Subscribe presence rate                                                                   |
| `INITIAL_SUBSCRIBE_RATIO`  | No        | `0.02`                      | Initial subscribe ratio                                                                   |
| `INITIAL_SUBSCRIBE_MIN`    | No        | `4`                         | Initial subscribe minimum                                                                 |
| `ROOM_ID`                  | No        | `rid-__prefix__-__count__`  | Value used to generate room ids during `populate`                                         |
| `USER_ID`                  | No        | `uid-__prefix__-__count__`  | Value used to generate user ids during `populate`                                         |
| `SSL_ENABLED`              | No        | `no`                        | Rocket.Chat server has SSL or not                                                         |
| `CLIENT_TYPE`              | No        | `web`                       | Which client will be simulated (changes the APIs used). Can be: `web`, `android` or `ios` |
| `USERS_EMAIL`              | No        | `@domain.com`               | User's email domain used to register                                                      |
| `LOG_IN`                   | No        | `yes`                       | If clients should log in or just connect                                                  |
| `IGNORE_ROOMS`             | No        | `GENERAL`                   | Comma-separated list of rooms to ignore                                                   |
| `USERS_PER_ROOM`           | No        | `10`                        | Number of users per room                                                                  |
| `SUBSCRIPTION_ID`          | No        | `sib-__rid__-__uid__`       | Template for subscription IDs                                                             |
| `TASK_ID`                  | No        | `1` or network address      | Task identifier, used to differentiate between multiple load tester instances             |
| `CLUSTER_GROUP`            | No        | `loadtester`                | Name of the cluster group                                                                 |
| `MESSAGE`                  | No        | `hello`                     | Default message content to be sent                                                        |
| `ROUTING_CONFIG_PER_SEC`   | No        | `10`                        | Routing configurations per second                                                         |
| `QUEUED_INQUIRIES_PER_SEC` | No        | `0.5`                       | Rate of queued inquiries per second                                                       |
| `TAKE_INQUIRY_PER_SEC`     | No        | `1`                         | Rate of taking inquiries per second                                                       |
| `DYNAMIC_LOGIN`            | No        | `false`                     | Enable dynamic login behavior (accepts 'true' or 'yes')                                   |

global:
  scrape_interval:     15s # By default, scrape targets every 15 seconds.
  evaluation_interval: 15s # Evaluate rules every 15 seconds.
  # Attach these extra labels to all timeseries collected by this Prometheus instance.
  external_labels:
    monitor: 'codelab-monitor'
rule_files:
  - 'prometheus.rules'
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'prometheus'
    scrape_interval: 5s
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9090']
  - job_name: 'load-tester'
    # DNS service discovery, not a static target: with `docker compose up --scale load-scale=N`
    # the service name resolves to one A record per container. A static target only ever scrapes
    # whichever single container DNS answers with, so every other loader stays invisible and the
    # dashboard silently reports a fraction of the real load.
    dns_sd_configs:
      - names:
          - load-scale
        type: A
        port: 4000
        refresh_interval: 15s

apiVersion: 1

datasources:
  - name: Prometheus
    type: prometheus
    access: proxy
    url: http://prometheus:9090
    isDefault: true
    editable: true

FROM node:20 as builder

COPY . /app

WORKDIR /app

RUN npm install \
    && npm run build \
    && cp package.json /app/dist/

ENV NODE_ENV=production

RUN cd /app/dist && npm install

FROM node:20-alpine

COPY --from=builder /app/dist/ /app

WORKDIR /app

ENV PORT=4000 \
    NODE_ENV=production \
    DEBUG=app:server

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["node", "cjs/index.js"]
